daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Former President Jokowi publicly denied that his participation in a traditional buffalo head-stepping ceremony carried any political meaning, addressing speculation about symbolic political messages in his post-presidential activities. Separately, a controversy emerged over the use of diplomatic passports and travel budgets after questions were raised about the Public Works Minister's family traveling to the US on official missions. Meanwhile, an MPR deputy chair questioned claims that MPR Secretary General Ahmad Muzani was officially assigned by the government to visit Iran, with another legislator stating the president cannot order an MPR chair to undertake such missions.

  • The KPK is investigating alleged money flows from Kuantan Singingi Regency head to Forestry Minister Raja Juli Antoni, with investigators stating the minister should have immediately reported the gratuity after receiving an envelope, while the KPK also alleges the Kuansing regent extorted 914 farmers for forest area permits.
  • Commission II of the DPR does not yet know when debate on the election law revision will begin, while an electoral expert stated the KPU-Bawaslu selection team must be formed before October 2026, and a Democrat legislator called for close monitoring of the election bill discussions.
  • DPR Speaker Puan Maharani recalled Sukarno's legacy during her meeting with Indian Prime Minister Modi, while Indonesia and India agreed to strengthen parliamentary cooperation and share responsibility for regional stability.
  • A court granted a lawsuit by Human Rights Ministry employees against Minister Beka Ulung Hapsara (Pigai), while the minister stated his office will not form an investigation team into the death of a pregnant woman in Papua.
  • A judge partially granted Roy Suryo's pretrial motion, ruling his arrest in the case involving Jokowi's academic credentials was unlawful, with former president Jokowi stating he will attend the trial and present his diplomas from elementary school through university.
  • The Hajj Minister proposed 2027 Hajj costs of Rp 107.3 million, an increase of Rp 19 million from 2026.
  • The Religious Affairs Ministry will include LGBT prevention material in the curriculum, while the Home Affairs Ministry responded to a proposal to rename West Java Province to Tatar Sunda.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia and India finalized a BrahMos missile procurement agreement during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's state visit, with India stating the cooperation aims to enhance defense self-reliance. President Prabowo awarded Modi the Bintang Adipurna, Indonesia's highest honor, with Modi expressing deep honor at receiving the decoration. The two leaders also agreed to develop a strategic port partnership connecting Sabang and the Andaman Islands, while launching Prambanan temple restoration cooperation and declaring a Tagore-Ki Hajar Dewantara year.

  • President Prabowo stated democracy is not an easy path but the best system for justice during Modi's visit, and described himself as an admirer of Modi at an Indian community reception.
  • Indonesia and India agreed to link QRIS and UPI payment systems with India hoping integration will be completed by end-2026, while Prabowo supported establishing IIM and IIT campuses in Indonesia to boost bilateral education ties.
  • The two countries reaffirmed support for a Two-State solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict and pledged to champion Global South interests in international forums.
  • Iran is waiting for the right time to confirm a visit by an Indonesian delegation, with Iran's ambassador stating solidarity for Supreme Leader Khamenei represents deep Indonesia-Iran ties.
  • Indonesia and Singapore relations have reached a new high with growing trust between the two countries.

Other

Four state-owned asset management companies officially completed their merger, consolidating the sector under a unified BUMN structure. The Environment Minister called for "ecological repentance" through mangrove rehabilitation, as Indonesia promoted mangrove restoration to heal the environment. Meanwhile, the government is building 20 new hospitals and upgrading 66 facilities to strengthen the healthcare system.

  • The Ministry of Communication clarified that biometric SIM card registration is voluntary for existing users, with mobile operators required to pay Rp 3,000 for each biometric registration of customer SIM cards.
  • Coordinating Minister Zulhas introduced Lahsamor technology from BRIN to address organic waste in Bali, while the government is developing an Early Warning System to protect consumers.
  • India will supply affordable, high-quality medicines to Indonesia, while nearly all Indonesian pilgrims received outpatient care during the Hajj season.
  • A severe drought is affecting multiple areas across Java, leaving thousands of residents struggling to access clean water.
  • The Papua provincial government donated 60 Starlink devices to Jayapura Regency to expand internet access, while Indonesia unveiled SBIN at INNOPROM 2026 to attract Eurasian investment.
